name: Arlington EATS
description: Arlington EATS is a community-focused nonprofit working to eliminate food insecurity for Arlington residents. The organization provides consistent access to nutritious food through weekly markets, home deliveries, and school-based programs. Families with young children benefit from wraparound support, including essentials such as diapers and hygiene products. Arlington EATS partners closely with community groups to strengthen local food distribution networks. Their mission emphasizes dignity, choice, and equitable access for every household they serve.

name: Diaper Depot
description: Diaper Depot is a local resource dedicated specifically to addressing diaper need for families struggling to afford essential infant supplies. The organization distributes diapers, wipes, and related care items through coordinated community events and partnerships with social-service agencies. Their work helps alleviate financial stress for caregivers, allowing families to redirect limited income toward other critical needs such as food and housing. Diaper Depot emphasizes reliability, compassion, and accessibility in their service model. By partnering with groups like the Beantown Baby Diaper Bank, they expand their reach to more vulnerable families.

name: Family ACCESS
description: Family ACCESS supports children and families by providing early childhood education, family support services, and community resources. The organization offers programs that strengthen early development, promote school readiness, and empower caregivers with practical tools. Many families they serve face economic hardship, and Family ACCESS helps meet basic needs by distributing essentials such as diapers. Their holistic approach promotes both emotional well-being and economic stability for families. Through collaborative partnerships, Family ACCESS reaches households across multiple communities.

name: Lexington Food Pantry
description: The Lexington Food Pantry provides critical food assistance to residents experiencing financial hardship. Operating through a volunteer-driven model, the pantry distributes fresh produce, shelf-stable goods, and personal-care essentials—including diapers—to eligible families. The organization focuses on creating a respectful, welcoming environment for all clients. By leveraging donations from individuals, faith communities, and local businesses, they maintain dependable weekly services. Their long-standing presence in Lexington makes them a trusted support system for families in need.

name: Margaret Fuller Neighborhood House
description: The Margaret Fuller Neighborhood House offers a wide range of community services, including a food pantry, youth programming, and family support initiatives. Located in Cambridge, the organization serves diverse residents facing financial, social, or housing challenges. Their pantry supplies food, diapers, and other vital necessities to families seeking stability. With a mission rooted in empowerment and community connection, the organization works to reduce inequality and strengthen neighborhood resilience. Their partnerships with other local nonprofits help expand their impact across the region.

name: Middlesex Human Service Agency (MHSA)
description: MHSA provides housing, shelter, food assistance, and supportive services to individuals and families experiencing homelessness or economic insecurity. Their programs aim to promote long-term stability through case management, recovery support, and basic-needs distribution. Families with infants or toddlers receive essential care items—including diapers—to help ease the financial strain of raising young children. MHSA’s work is grounded in dignity, compassion, and evidence-based support practices. As a key regional service provider, they collaborate with many community organizations to address the root causes of poverty.

name: People Helping People- Burlington Food Pantry
description: People Helping People is a Burlington-based nonprofit dedicated to reducing hunger and supporting local families in crisis. Their food pantry distributes nutritious groceries, household supplies, and infant essentials such as diapers. The organization also operates seasonal programs, including holiday meals and back-to-school support. Volunteers play a central role in ensuring that services run efficiently and compassionately. People Helping People fosters a strong sense of community and ensures that every resident has access to fundamental resources.

name: Project SOUP - Somerville Homeless Coalition
description: Project SOUP ("Share Our United Pantry") is a long-standing Somerville food-access program offering free groceries through its pantry and home-delivery services. As part of the Somerville Homeless Coalition, Project SOUP addresses homelessness, hunger, and economic instability. The program serves individuals and families of all ages, providing both food and essential items like diapers. Their community-driven model emphasizes dignity, choice, and reducing barriers to support. Project SOUP remains a vital resource for residents facing hardship.

name: REACH Beyond Domestic Violence
description: REACH Beyond Domestic Violence provides critical services to individuals and families impacted by domestic abuse, including shelter, advocacy, and long-term support. Many survivors arrive with limited belongings, and REACH supplies essentials such as diapers, clothing, and hygiene products to help stabilize families. Their trauma-informed approach prioritizes safety, empowerment, and respect. REACH also engages in community education to prevent future violence. Their partnership work allows them to connect clients with broader regional resources for continued support.

name: Tufts Wakefield/Melrose
description: Tufts Wakefield/Melrose operates community clinics and health services that support families across the region. Their programs assist caregivers navigating medical, financial, and social challenges. In partnership with regional nonprofits, the clinics distribute diapers and child-care essentials to families encountering hardship. Staff members are trained to identify unmet household needs and connect families to supportive services. This integrated model ensures that medical care and basic-needs assistance work hand-in-hand.

name: Watertown Food Pantry
description: The Watertown Food Pantry offers weekly food distribution for residents experiencing financial stress. Alongside groceries, the pantry provides diapers and personal-care items to help families meet essential needs. Their program relies on strong volunteer engagement and consistent community donations. The pantry’s mission emphasizes dignity, confidentiality, and neighbor-to-neighbor support. Over time, it has become a reliable safety net for Watertown households.

name: WeeCare
description: WeeCare focuses on supporting families with infants and toddlers by providing diapers, wipes, and early childhood essentials. Their programs help reduce the severe financial burden associated with diaper need, especially for low-income households. WeeCare works with local service agencies to reach families who may not have access to traditional support systems. They emphasize compassion, accessibility, and reducing stigma around requesting help. Their efforts help ensure that every baby has the resources necessary for healthy development.

name: Woburn Council of Social Concern
description: The Council of Social Concern serves Woburn and surrounding communities through its food pantry, early education center, and family-support programs. Their pantry distributes diapers and household necessities alongside groceries, relieving pressure on families with young children. The organization also offers parenting programs and child-care services that strengthen family stability. With a focus on compassion and practical assistance, the Council has been a trusted resource for decades. Partnerships with regional nonprofits help them expand their reach and impact.

name: Riverside Early Headstart
description: Riverside Early Head Start provides comprehensive early childhood and family support services to infants, toddlers, and expectant parents. Their programs focus on strengthening child development, promoting school readiness, and supporting families with social, emotional, and economic needs. Through home-based visits and center-based care, Riverside offers individualized developmental support and access to health and nutrition resources. Families can also receive diapers and other essentials as part of their holistic services. The organization emphasizes equity, family empowerment, and early intervention to ensure every child has the foundation they need to thrive.

name: United South End Settlement
description: United South End Settlements is a long-standing Boston nonprofit dedicated to supporting children, families, and communities through education, workforce development, and social-service programs. USES focuses especially on breaking the cycle of poverty by giving families access to childcare, youth enrichment programs, and economic-mobility services. Many families served face significant financial strain, and USES helps meet basic needs by distributing essentials such as diapers. Their family-centered model promotes stability, growth, and long-term opportunity. With deep community roots, USES plays a key role in strengthening the social fabric of the South End and surrounding neighborhoods.

name: Kataluma Refugee Hospitality
description: Kataluma Refugee Hospitality provides temporary housing, community support, and relational care for individuals and families seeking asylum or transitioning out of refugee status. Their hospitality homes create a safe, stable living environment where guests can rebuild their lives with dignity. Kataluma partners with volunteers, faith communities, and social-service organizations to offer mentorship, case support, and essential items—including diapers for families with young children. Their model centers on compassion, cultural understanding, and empowerment. By fostering community connections, Kataluma helps refugees establish independence and belonging in the Greater Boston area.

name: Gandara Center
description: The Gándara Center offers behavioral health, substance-use treatment, and family-support services to culturally diverse communities across Massachusetts. Originally founded to serve the Latino community, the organization now provides multilingual, culturally responsive care to individuals of all backgrounds. Their programs include outpatient counseling, residential treatment, youth services, and family-stabilization support. Families facing financial hardship may also receive basic necessities such as diapers and hygiene items. The Gándara Center is committed to promoting wellness, recovery, and resilience through accessible and inclusive care.

name: Phoenix House NE
description: Phoenix House New England provides comprehensive residential and outpatient services for individuals recovering from substance-use disorders. Their programs support adults, teens, and families through evidence-based treatment, counseling, and recovery-support services. Many clients are parents working toward stability, and Phoenix House helps meet practical needs—including diapers for young children—to reduce stress during recovery. Their person-centered approach emphasizes dignity, long-term healing, and family reconnection. As one of the region’s major treatment networks, Phoenix House plays a vital role in addressing addiction and supporting community wellness.

name: Allways Health
description: AllWays Health Partners (formerly Neighborhood Health Plan) is a Massachusetts-based health insurance provider offering affordable, community-focused coverage. In collaboration with healthcare systems and community organizations, AllWays supports families by connecting them to essential services, preventive care, and wellness programs. Their commitment to health equity includes supporting initiatives that address social determinants of health, such as food security and diaper need. By partnering with local nonprofits, AllWays helps broaden access to critical resources for families with young children. The organization emphasizes high-quality care, customer support, and community impact.
